external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor node installed at a customer site.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside our physical control. Each node has a shared fleet pre-shared key; the source does not state whether the node stores it.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker that receives readings from sensor nodes and forwards accepted readings.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE
processes.notes: The broker uses a pre-shared key per fleet. Nobody has rotated it since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer that picks up readings and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check device keys and identify the customer associated with a node.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A messaging service carrying readings from the device gateway to the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery store containing sensor telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not say whether firmware images are signed.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: A sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up a device in the device registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: device identity, key, and customer association

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll firmware
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read because making the nodes authenticate to it was awkward.

data_flows.name: service nodes
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer sites
trust_boundaries.description: Customer-controlled sites where sensor nodes are installed and serviced.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The analytics network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators view dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The sensor node is placed in the customer-sites trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source says sensor nodes are installed on customer sites.

assumptions.assumption: The field technician is placed in the customer-sites trust boundary while servicing nodes.
assumptions.basis: The source says field technicians service nodes over a local serial console, and the nodes are installed on customer sites.

assumptions.assumption: The fleet operator is placed in the corporate-network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source says fleet operators view dashboards from the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The customer-sites boundary is controlled by a different party and is therefore a tenant boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the sites as customer sites outside the system owner's physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The analytics-network boundary is a network boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source names an analytics network where the telemetry normalizer runs.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate-network boundary is a network boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source names the corporate network used by fleet operators.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as an MQTT broker.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: It is described as a Python consumer.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential because it holds keys and customer associations.
assumptions.basis: The source says the registry is used to check the key and identify which customer a node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: The Pub/Sub store is confidential because it carries sensor readings that are customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source says accepted readings are forwarded onto Pub/Sub, and the telemetry lake containing such data is customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns, described as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source says the lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns and is customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The firmware bucket is public because the source says it is public read.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly says the bucket is public read.

assumptions.assumption: Sensor readings are personal data because they are readings tied to deployed customer devices and the resulting lake contains customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source describes readings from sensor nodes and identifies the resulting telemetry as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway holds credentials and personal data because it authenticates nodes and processes their readings and customer associations.
assumptions.basis: The source says the gateway uses a fleet pre-shared key, checks device keys, identifies customers, and accepts readings.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry holds credentials and personal data because it stores or provides the key and customer association used by the gateway.
assumptions.basis: The source says the registry is queried to check the key and find which customer the node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: The Pub/Sub store holds personal data because it carries accepted sensor readings.
assumptions.basis: The source says accepted readings are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and later written to the customer-data lake.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer holds personal data because it picks up and writes sensor readings.
assumptions.basis: The source says the normalizer picks up readings and writes them into the telemetry lake.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake holds personal data because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly identifies those contents as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The firmware bucket holds business-critical data because it stores firmware images used to update deployed nodes.
assumptions.basis: The source says nodes poll the bucket for a new firmware image and install it.
